# Code Principles

## Core: "Code is not an asset, it is a liability"
The asset is the behavior. Code is the cost. Every line must be read, understood, debugged, updated, and can break.

## Reduction Rules
- Delete unused code — Git has history.
- Delete commented-out code.
- When a feature is superseded, delete old code in the same PR.
- Actively hunt dead code when touching a file.
- Prefer deleting lines over adding lines when behavior stays the same.

## Abstraction & Duplication
- Extract on first duplication (2 call sites = extract).
- Don't add helpers "in case we need them."
- Don't add config options for flexibility — hardcode, add the option when the second use case arrives.

## Error Handling
- Only validate at system boundaries (user input, API responses, DB reads). Trust internal code.
- Don't handle edge cases that can't currently happen — add handling when the case becomes real.

## Comments
- Minimal comments only when completely necessary. Code should be self-explanatory.
- Never comment-out code. Never explain WHAT code does — the code itself should say that.

## Naming
- Named constants over magic numbers/strings, always — even single-use. The name IS the documentation.
- Boolean prefixes: `is`, `has`, `can`, `should` (e.g. `isLoading`, `hasPermission`, `canEdit`).
- Descriptive names for unused params (`_unusedEvent` over `_`).

## Style
- `const`-first — use `let` only when reassignment is needed.
- Early returns / guard clauses — avoid deep nesting.
- Ternary ONLY for simple value assignment (`const x = cond ? a : b`). Everything else uses if/else.
- Direct imports — no barrel files (index.ts re-exports).

## Size Limits
- File: ~800 lines max → refactor is imminent.
- Function/method: ~35 lines max → extract.

## Design
- Apply SOLID and DRY. Use design patterns where they offer utility.

## Folder Architecture ("Use the app → find the code")
The folder tree mirrors UI navigation. Using the app once = knowing where code lives.

```
src/app/
├── pages/           ← one folder per navigable page (flat siblings, no admin/ nesting)
│   └── {page}/
│       ├── {sub-page}/   ← sub-pages as subfolders (e.g. chat/, tasks/)
│       ├── helpers/      ← page-specific services (only used by this page)
│       ├── dialogs/      ← page-specific dialogs
├── services/        ← multi-page services (used by 2+ pages)
│   ├── auth/        ← auth, profile, guards
│   ├── data/        ← firestore facades (user, project, donor...)
│   └── ui/          ← right-panel, dialog-back, mobile-sidebar, title...
├── components/      ← reusable UI (shared components, directives, pipes)
├── models/          ← all interfaces/types grouped by domain (project.model, donor.model...)
```

**Rules:**
- Service used only by its page → `pages/{page}/helpers/`
- Used by 2+ pages → `services/`
- All models in top-level `models/` (dependency arrow: pages → services → models)
- No admin/ grouping — all pages are flat siblings in pages/
- Reusable UI components → `components/`

# Mistakes to Avoid

> Feature-specific pitfalls have been moved to the relevant `.github/instructions/*.instructions.md` files (angular-components, mobile, chat, cloud-functions, testing). Only universal items remain here.

## Behavioral
- **NEVER run recursive PowerShell scripts** like `Get-ChildItem -Recurse | ForEach-Object { Get-Content ... }` — this instantly freezes VS Code. Use `grep_search`, `file_search`, or `read_file` tools instead. Also avoid `Select-String -Recurse` on large trees.
- **E2E tests must show live progress**: Never pipe Playwright output to `Out-String` or use `mode=sync`. Always use `mode=async` so the user sees real-time progress in the terminal.
- **Never hallucinate about external apps.** Say "I don't know" if unsure.
- **Never claim to have "checked the internet"** unless actually fetching a webpage.
- **Ask mobile or desktop first** before debugging layout/alignment issues.
- **Don't auto-update docs** — user confirms via `/update-docs` prompt.
- **Always deploy after code changes** — never leave changes undeployed. Build + `firebase deploy --only hosting --force` immediately after every code edit.
- **Revert failed attempts in the SAME deploy as the fix.**
- **One hypothesis at a time.** Max 3 attempts of the same category — then switch approach.

## E2E / Playwright
- **WebKit CI needs Playwright container**: Use `mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.60.0-noble` container for reliable WebKit deps. Standard ubuntu-latest has incomplete WebKit support.
- **WebKit Touch/ContextMenu in mobile emulation**: Playwright's WebKit with iPhone emulation can't construct `Touch()`/`TouchEvent()` (Illegal constructor) and `dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent('contextmenu'))` doesn't trigger Angular bindings. Context menu tests must `test.skip()` on WebKit via `'none'` return from `openMobileContextMenu()`. Real iPhones use native touch — this is a Playwright limitation, not an app bug.
- **Hover action buttons intercepted by adjacent messages**: Fixed via `z-index: 3` on `.message:hover` in `chat.component.scss` — creates stacking context so hover action buttons aren't intercepted by adjacent messages. No `force: true` needed. Must be > 2 (reactions-row z-index) so the emoji picker inside the hovered message stays above other messages' reaction chips.
- **Stacking context traps child z-index values**: When a parent has `z-index` (creating a stacking context), ALL descendants' z-index values are trapped within it. The emoji picker (`z-index: 1000`) inside `.message:hover { z-index: 1 }` was rendered BELOW adjacent reactions (`z-index: 2`) because 1 < 2 in the parent context. Fix: ensure message hover z-index > reactions z-index.
- **`isolation: isolate` causes hover paint loops**: Adding `isolation: isolate` to `main` (grid container) while `.message:hover` toggles z-index creates rapid repaint cycles — the stacking context boundary triggers relayout on each hover frame. Use `position: relative; z-index: 0` on `:host` (app-root) instead for defense-in-depth against CDK overlay competition.
- **Scroll assertions after async operations need polling, not fixed waits**: ResizeObserver + Angular rendering race means `waitForTimeout(500)` is unreliable for scroll position checks. Use `waitForFunction(() => el.scrollHeight - el.scrollTop - el.clientHeight < threshold, null, { timeout: 5000 })`.
- **Scroll-to-bottom button click needs waitForScrollStable**: The button click triggers a `scrollTo` with `behavior: 'smooth'` — measuring `scrollTop` immediately after gives stale values (gap = 8587px instead of <150). Always add `waitForScrollStable()` (RAF-based `scrollTop` convergence check) after programmatic scroll before asserting position.
- **Scroll-to-top in beforeEach needs retry loop**: Real-time Firestore listeners may auto-scroll back to bottom after `scrollTop = 0`. Use a loop that sets `scrollTop = 0`, waits 1s, checks gap, and repeats up to 5 times.
- **@mention popup shows raw UIDs before userNameMap resolves**: Add a `waitForTimeout(500)` before typing filter text, and don't assert on specific user names that depend on async data loading.
- **Textarea highlight overlay jump**: When adding a backdrop div behind a transparent textarea for styled text (e.g. bold mentions), do NOT apply `position: relative; z-index; background: transparent` unconditionally to the textarea — only apply when the overlay is active (e.g. via `.has-mention-overlay` class). Unconditional styles shift the text rendering layout. Also: `overflow: hidden` on the popup container overrides `overflow-y: auto` — so scrolling won't work even if `max-height` is set.

## Testing
- **AngularFire JIT errors in unit tests**: If a spec imports a module that transitively imports `@angular/fire/firestore`, the Angular unit-test builder throws JIT compilation errors. Fix: extract pure functions (e.g. `getLang`, `getLocale`) into a dependency-free file (`active-lang.ts`) and import from there. Don't try `vi.mock` for relative imports — the builder blocks it.
- **Angular test builder blocks `vi.mock` for relative imports**: The `@angular/build:unit-test` vitest-mock-patch rejects `vi.mock('./relative-path')`. Only non-relative module specifiers (`@angular/fire/firestore`, `@angular/fire/auth`, `@shared/time-constants.json`) can be mocked. For services with Angular DI, use `Object.create(Service.prototype)` + manual property assignment to bypass `inject()` calls. Do NOT mock `@angular/core` — `vi.mock("@angular/core", async () => importActual(...))` causes "Cannot access before initialization" errors due to hoisting + async import circular reference.
- **`@shared/*` path alias needs explicit mock**: The `tsconfig.json` alias `@shared/* → functions/shared/*` is resolved by esbuild during Angular test builds. If a transitive import hits `@shared/time-constants.json`, mock it with `vi.mock("@shared/time-constants.json", () => ({ default: { ... } }))` — the factory must return a `default` export since it's a JSON import.

## Firestore Queries
- **Async recompute races with navigation**: `recomputeUnread()` checks `recentlyVisited` at the start, but the async `computeUnreadCount()` call takes a network round-trip. If `handleNavigation()` fires during that gap (zeros count + adds to `recentlyVisited`), the async result overwrites the zero. Fix: re-check `recentlyVisited` AFTER the `await` — not just before. Also: `computeUnreadCount` must subtract the user's own messages (`senderId == uid`) to prevent phantom badges caused by client/server clock drift exceeding `MARK_READ_SKEW_MS`.
- **DM list must use `trackEntity()` like projects/skills**: Manual dual subscriptions (latestMessage$ + readState$) miss the `getActiveId` guard that prevents recomputing unread for the currently-viewed conversation. Always use `UnreadTrackingService.trackEntity()` for all three sections.
- **Collection queries with per-document rules fail for non-privileged users**: A `where("chapterId", "==", X)` query on `projects` is rejected for regular users because Firestore rules require `uid in resource.data.members` — Firestore can't prove the constraint is satisfied without reading every doc. - **Non-overflowing initial load blocks pagination permanently**: The anchor strategy (`startWithAnchor`) loads only `CONTEXT_SIZE = 10` messages before `lastReadAt`. Fix: `loadOlderIfNotOverflowing()` runs after initial render and recursively loads older pages until content overflows or no more exist. Most visible in DMs with short messages.

## Cloud Functions
- **User name resolution must prefer `displayName`**: The `displayName` field is the user's chosen name (set during onboarding — could be a nickname like "Zumi" or a properly formatted full name like "Kovács Nóra" for Hungarian). Wrap each operation with `.catch(e => logger.error(...))` so failures are logged but don't crash the trigger.

## CSS Grid
- **Single-column grid with multiple items targeting same column**: When `grid-template-columns` collapses to `1fr` (e.g. `.no-nav` mode) and multiple items have `grid-column: 1` without explicit `grid-row`, CSS Grid auto-places them into separate rows. Only the first explicit row (`1fr`) gets full height — subsequent implicit rows are `auto`-sized (content height only). Fix: add `grid-row: 1` to the item that needs full height. The mobile breakpoint already had this fix.

## Scroll Anchoring
- **`overflow-anchor: none` on a scroll target causes content-shift drift**: If the user scrolls to an element (e.g. unread separator via `scrollIntoView({ block: 'start' })`), but that element has `overflow-anchor: none`, the browser picks a *different* element as its scroll anchor (typically the first child below). When content above the separator loads and expands (images, link previews), the browser adjusts scroll to keep the anchor (not the separator) stable — the separator drifts up. Fix: temporarily set `overflow-anchor: auto` on the target element during the grace period. Clear it on user-initiated scroll so normal anchoring resumes. Distinguish programmatic scrolls from user gestures via a brief flag cleared on next rAF.

## Cross-Platform
- **Windows doesn't render flag emojis**: Flag emoji characters (🇬🇧 🇭🇺) display as two-letter country codes on Windows (Edge, Chrome, Firefox). Use inline SVGs for flags instead of emoji. macOS/iOS/Android render them fine.
- **Desktop OS notification toasts truncate after ~3 body lines**: Windows (Action Center) and macOS show only ~3 lines of notification body text. If SW stacking shows more (e.g. 5 visible messages), the OS truncates and the `+N earlier` count doesn't match what's actually readable. Keep `MAX_VISIBLE = 2` so body = "+N earlier" + 2 messages = 3 lines max, fitting the OS toast perfectly.

Fix: import from `firebase/firestore` + `firebase/app` directly and use `getFirestore(getApp())` — always returns the real registered instance regardless of Angular DI state.
- **`content-visibility: auto` breaks scroll positioning**: Applying `content-visibility: auto` + `contain-intrinsic-block-size: auto 80px` to chat message bubbles causes scrollbar flickering and incorrect initial scroll position. The `auto` keyword caches rendered size after first paint, but during initial load the estimated 80px doesn't match actual bubble heights (50–400px) — the browser shifts scroll position each time a bubble enters the viewport and gets its real size. Combined with `overflow-anchor: auto`, this creates competing scroll adjustments. Pure CSS "free rendering skip" doesn't work with scroll-to-position-on-load patterns. Use only if messages have fixed known heights.
- **`overflow-anchor` is unreliable for scroll pinning**: Safari/WebKit has ZERO `overflow-anchor` support. Firefox has suppression triggers (adding a class that changes computed properties disables anchoring for that frame). Never rely on CSS `overflow-anchor` alone for critical scroll position maintenance. Use JavaScript: detect drift via `getBoundingClientRect()` comparison and call `scrollIntoView({ block: 'start' })` to re-pin. The `rescrollToSeparator()` pattern checks if the target element drifted >5px from expected position and corrects only when needed — avoids fighting user scroll (content below target loading doesn't cause drift, so no correction fires).
- **Grace period must start immediately in separator path**: If `handleInitialLoad()` sets `firstUnreadMsgId` + `initialScrolledToSeparator` but defers `startScrollGracePeriod()` to a later flush, iOS layout-triggered scroll events fire in between — `handleScroll` sees `isUserNearBottom=true` + `initialScrollGracePeriod=false` and clears `firstUnreadMsgId`. Always start the grace period in the same call that sets the separator state.
- **Deep-unread requires "load around anchor" pattern**: When user has 100+ unread, a single `limitToLast(30)` realtime query loads only the newest 30 (all unread) with no read-boundary context. Fixed with `startWithAnchor(lastReadAt)`: two parallel `getDocs` (context `endAt(lastReadAt) + limitToLast(10)` + unread `startAfter(lastReadAt) + limit(30)`), merged and deduplicated by ID, sorted by timestamp. A tail realtime listener (`startAfter(newestLoadedTs)`) then handles new messages. No backfill loop needed.
- **Read receipts render async and shift bottom position**: `readState` subscription arrives after initial `scrollToBottom()` fires. The ~17px (16px avatar + 1px padding) of read receipt avatars below the last message pushes the previous "bottom" above the viewport. Fix: in the `onUpdate` callback from `ChatReadReceiptService`, call `scrollToBottom()` during the initial scroll grace period when user is near bottom. `overflow-anchor: auto` alone doesn't fix this because the anchor is a message above — the new content appears below the anchor.
- **iOS Safari doesn't reliably fire `contextmenu` on long-press**: The native `contextmenu` DOM event is unreliable on iOS — especially when elements contain `<img>` tags (triggers native image callout) or use CDK drag-drop with competing touch delays. All list rows using `ContextMenuHelper` + `(contextmenu)` must also have `appLongPress`. The directive adds `-webkit-touch-callout: none` and runs listeners outside Angular zone. Also add `pointer-events: none` on `<img>` elements inside list rows to prevent them from stealing the gesture.
- **Chrome Mobile `setSelectionRange` throws DOMException "illegal access"**: On Android Chrome (especially older versions like Android 10), calling `textarea.setSelectionRange()` on an unfocused element throws a DOMException. Wrap all `setSelectionRange` calls in a `safeSetSelectionRange(el, start, end)` helper that catches and silently ignores the error. The cursor position is cosmetic — losing it is acceptable.
- **Firestore real-time arrays can contain `undefined` entries**: During network instability or cache corruption, `collectionData()` can emit arrays with undefined items. Defensive `filter(Boolean)` should be applied at the data-layer level (`FirestoreRepository.allDocs$()`, shared data services) — not just at subscription sites.
- **`Notification.requestPermission()` must be first await on mobile**: Mobile browsers (especially Chrome Android) require `Notification.requestPermission()` to be called in the same synchronous microtask as the user's tap. Any `await` before it (e.g. `await waitForInit()`) breaks the user-activation chain — the browser silently ignores the permission prompt with no dialog, no error.
- **PWA manifest `"orientation"` doesn't lock on Android Chrome**: The `"orientation": "portrait"` field in `manifest.webmanifest` is a hint that Chrome ignores for installed PWAs. Must call `screen.orientation.lock('portrait')` programmatically when `display-mode: standalone` matches. Use `(screen.orientation as any)?.lock?.()` — TypeScript's `ScreenOrientation` type doesn't include `lock`.
- **`-webkit-user-select` needed on mobile**: Android Chrome requires the `-webkit-` prefix for `user-select: none` to work. Always set both: `-webkit-user-select: none; user-select: none;`. Restore `user-select: text` (with prefix) on `input`/`textarea` elements.
- **`blurOnKeyboardClose()` needs growth threshold + focus grace period on iOS**: The `visualViewport.resize` handler that blurs inputs when the keyboard closes must check for significant height growth (>100px), not any growth. On iOS Safari, the autocorrect/predictive text bar and `100dvh` recalculations cause small viewport height fluctuations during normal typing. Without a threshold, every keystroke triggers blur → keyboard dismiss → reopen cycle. Typical keyboard height is 250–350px, so 100px threshold safely distinguishes toolbar adjustments from full keyboard close. Additionally: a 600ms grace period after `focusin` is required — iOS sends transient positive viewport deltas during keyboard *open* animation that exceed 100px and would trigger blur.
- **iOS WebKit resigns first responder on sibling programmatic scroll**: On iOS Safari, calling `scrollTop = N` or `scrollTo()` on a sibling element while the keyboard is animating open causes WebKit to blur the focused textarea — the keyboard appears then immediately dismisses. Fix: skip all programmatic scroll adjustments in viewport resize handlers when `document.activeElement` is an input/textarea. The scroll will correct itself naturally once the keyboard finishes animating.
- **ResizeObserver + keyboard = cumulative scroll drift**: A `ResizeObserver` that applies `scrollTop += delta` to compensate for container height changes (e.g. top bar appearing) will mis-adjust during keyboard open/close — the container shrinks/grows from the **bottom** (via `100dvh` chain), not the top. Height-comparison detection races with `visualViewport` resize handler. Fix: use a `viewportResizing` boolean flag set by `visualViewport` resize handler (cleared 400ms after last event). ResizeObserver checks the flag and skips delta during keyboard animation.
- **iOS video thumbnails need `playsinline` + no `opacity: 0` fade-in**: iOS Safari ignores `preload="metadata"` on `<video>` elements, so `loadeddata` never fires. If CSS starts video at `opacity: 0` waiting for a `.loaded` class, the thumbnail stays invisible. Fix: always add `playsinline` attribute to inline `<video>` elements, and don't use `opacity: 0` → `.loaded { opacity: 1 }` on videos — show them immediately with a dark background fallback. - **Race between `readState` subscription and `userNameMap$`**: The readState `collectionData` listener and the `users$` collection listener are independent Firestore queries. If readState arrives first, `userNameMap` is empty → avatars have no `photoURL`. Must call `refreshNames()` (rebuild readStates from rawReadStates) when userNameMap/userPhotoMap update, plus `tickAndDetect()` to push to OnPush children.
- **Production minification strips `if (!x) return` guards**: Angular's production optimizer can remove null-check early-return guards in component methods if the template types suggest null isn't possible. Use **optional chaining** (`task?.createdBy`) instead — `?.` compiles to a null-check that minifiers cannot strip.

Fix: add `position: relative` to `.read-receipts` so DOM order determines paint order. General rule: if two siblings overlap (negative margins, absolute children), ensure both have the same `position` type.
- **Fixed `CHARS_PER_LINE` in bubble collapse clips mobile messages**: `ChatBubbleCollapseService` estimated wrapping with a hardcoded 50 chars/line. On mobile, bubbles are ~255px wide (68% of 375px) and fit only ~25 chars/line — the service underestimated line count, didn't trigger "see more", and CSS `overflow-y: clip` silently truncated content. - **`overflow-y: clip` + fixed `max-height` clips variable-height content**: `.bubble-content` uses `overflow-y: clip` + `max-height` for collapse animation. When a link preview image or reply quote consumes part of the pixel budget, the "see more" link and text below get silently clipped.
